event.summary: A powerful explosion in the Plaka district of Athens, near the Acropolis, caused a two-storey building to collapse on September 25, 2026. At least two people were injured in the incident. The cause of the explosion is under investigation, with a gas leak suspected.

The incident occurred near the Acropolis, with four American tourists also reported dead. Rescuers have been working to recover victims from the collapsed structure.

timeline.title: Explosion in Athens' Plaka District Kills Six, Including Four American Tourists
timeline.summary: A suspected gas leak caused an explosion that leveled a two-storey residential building in the Plaka district of Athens, resulting in the deaths of six individuals, including four American tourists and two Greek residents. Emergency teams discovered the victims after the building collapsed shortly after the explosion, which occurred early in the morning. Greek authorities are investigating the incident to determine the cause of the explosion.

event_overview.title: About Building Collapse in Athens' Plaka Following Explosion Injures Two
event_overview.subject: Building Collapse in Athens' Plaka Following Explosion Injures Two
event_overview.summary: A two-storey building on Lysikratous Street in Athens’ historic Plaka district collapsed after an explosion shortly before 8 a.m. on September 25, 2026. The incident triggered a multi-agency rescue operation, caused damage to nearby properties, and remained under official investigation as of September 27; authorities had not publicly established the cause of the explosion.

facts.label: Date and location
facts.value: The explosion and collapse occurred shortly before 8 a.m. on September 25, 2026, at a two-storey house on Lysikratous Street in Plaka, central Athens.

facts.label: Casualties and rescues
facts.value: In a September 26 briefing, Greece’s Fire Service said six people had been recovered unconscious from the collapsed building and that two women were rescued from an adjacent building and taken by ambulance.

facts.label: Emergency response
facts.value: The search-and-rescue operation involved 30 firefighters, six vehicles including two specialist rescue vehicles, three search-and-rescue dogs, geophones and cameras; Athens municipal equipment assisted debris removal.

facts.label: Investigation
facts.value: The Fire Service’s Arson Crimes Division opened an ex officio preliminary investigation, under the direction of the Athens Court of First Instance prosecutor, to determine the sequence and causes of the explosion, fire and collapse. A reported gas smell prompted attendance by the gas-network operator, but officials had not confirmed a cause.

facts.label: Affected area
facts.value: The blast also damaged neighboring buildings and vehicles in Plaka, a historic district at the foot of the Acropolis and a major visitor area.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows major reported developments in the Plaka explosion and collapse, including changing casualty reports; it does not provide a final official cause, complete victim identification, or the full investigative and recovery record.
